_doc: Three-stream timeline of workflow evolution. The analyzer joins session.startTime against shippedAt/adoptedAt to compute per-session era tags emitted in metrics-by-era.json. Three streams keep agent-side rule edits (machine-extractable from git), user-side practice adoptions (manually authored at session wrap via Handoff Architect Phase 4 field #9), and infrastructure/tooling changes attributable independently. Retroactive seed dates are best-effort: agentRuleEdits derive precise timestamps from git log .github/instructions/; userPracticeAdoptions and infraToolingChanges use the earliest evidence date found in handoffs/ADRs/user-memory. Adoption-date precision claims no better than +/- 1 week for inferred entries. See ADR-0036.

agentRuleEdits.name: Pre-restructure baseline (monolith)
agentRuleEdits.description: Era-tagging anchor: prior to commit 48309ab the agent rules lived in .github/copilot-instructions.md as a single file. Sessions before 2026-05-28 fall in this era.

agentRuleEdits.name: Restructure into scoped skill files
agentRuleEdits.description: Split monolith into per-scope instruction files (compliance / logic / persistence / security / structural / ui). Established the file-per-concern shape every later rule edit assumes.

agentRuleEdits.name: Sharded docs/memory/ MCP graph backup
agentRuleEdits.description: Added shard-file backup layer under docs/memory/ so MCP graph corruption is recoverable from git history rather than a single JSONL file.

agentRuleEdits.name: Mandatory Post-Edit Scan gate
agentRuleEdits.description: After any file edit the agent must call get_errors on every modified file and fix any errors before handing back. Silently skipping the scan is a compliance failure.

agentRuleEdits.name: Workflow Logger skill + Phase 0 recipe lookup
agentRuleEdits.description: Added Workflow Logger to Phase 4 + an advisory Phase 0 step to check docs/workflows/ for a matching recipe before starting a task.
agentRuleEdits.source: persistence.instructions.md Workflow Logger, compliance.instructions.md Phase 0 step 0

agentRuleEdits.name: Confidence Trap + Symbol Check Gate + Memory Keeper hard gate
agentRuleEdits.description: Three rules: high confidence does not exempt the lookup stack; Symbol Check Gate forbids grep for symbol names; Memory Keeper must verify entity presence via open_nodes before any add_observations call.

agentRuleEdits.name: TDD as first-class Phase 2.5 skill
agentRuleEdits.description: Added Phase 2.5 RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for src/lib, src/app/api, src/data with mandatory verify steps. ADR-0018 captures the decision.

agentRuleEdits.name: Harden MCP memory infra + session continuity
agentRuleEdits.description: Locked the read-then-write Memory Keeper protocol with explicit open_nodes pre-check, shard-backup pairing, and session-continuity discipline at session start.

agentRuleEdits.name: Grep Gate (mandatory self-justification)
agentRuleEdits.description: Every grep_search invocation must include a one-line justification: Grep target is X, not a code symbol because Y. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Terminal-Echo Rule
agentRuleEdits.description: Terminal output echoed back as a user message must not trigger a new assistant turn unless exit code is non-zero or input is needed. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Phase 4 Composite Gate for handoff
agentRuleEdits.description: Handoff doc may only be written after Memory Keeper has run in the same response. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.
agentRuleEdits.source: persistence.instructions.md Handoff Architect Phase 4 Composite Gate

agentRuleEdits.name: Workflow Cadence Check (Phase 0 prelude)
agentRuleEdits.description: Every new session reads docs/chat-exports/analysis/workflow-reviews.json and surfaces days-since-last-review with on-cadence / due / overdue thresholds. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Handoff Architect Phase 4 field 8 (Workflow Review Cadence)
agentRuleEdits.description: Handoff doc must report days-since-last-review and append to workflow-reviews.json when this session performed a review. Phase 1 of the workflow self-improvement loop.

agentRuleEdits.name: Schema-Faithful Mocks rule 4 (Prisma checked/unchecked variant)
agentRuleEdits.description: Extends the 2026-06-22 Schema-Faithful Mocks skill with a new failure mode: Prisma at runtime selects between CreateInput (checked, relations as nested connect/create) and UncheckedCreateInput (unchecked, scalar FKs accepted) based on payload shape. An explicit `id` + scalar FK can trip the checked validator into demanding the relation form even though TS shows the unchecked variant accepting your shape. New rule: use `user: { connect: { id } }` form unconditionally when ambiguity is possible. Mocks cannot catch this — only live DB integration does. Reference incident: ADR-0051 Sprint α' Commit 2 (f3b36df).
agentRuleEdits.source: testing.instructions.md Schema-Faithful Mocks rule 4 + Red flag clause

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Session-start handoff read
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User adopted the practice of opening each session with a Session Start marker plus a summary of the most recent handoff. Codified shortly after into Handoff Architect CRITICAL clause.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Codegraph-first lookup discipline
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User explicitly flagged grep-for-symbol abuse as a recurring miss; established the codegraph_context / codegraph_search precedence over grep_search for symbol queries.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: E.T.C. (Execute -> Test -> Commit) ship rhythm
userPracticeAdoptions.description: Per-change atomic ETC cycle. ADHD-friendly: clear stages, completion signal after each, atomic commits stay revertible, test gate catches breakage before commit. Used as default ship rhythm on focused changes.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Verification-first bias
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When choosing between memory writes / docs / config tidying and end-to-end verification, default to verification. Lab evidence (real request, real DB, real UI) catches integration drift unit tests cannot.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Voice dictation for prompt authoring
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User started authoring prompts via voice dictation. Affects user-message length, syntax patterns, and the surface text the analyzer scans for negation regex.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Weekly workflow-review cadence
userPracticeAdoptions.description: User adopted a weekly cadence of analyzing chat exports, distilling friction patterns, and shipping rule edits before resuming feature work. Baseline 21-session review performed 2026-06-19.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Standalone-product framing for in-repo experiments
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When a system grows beyond a feature into something that could plausibly serve other tenants (Shipyard is the first instance), explicitly treat the current repo as the incubator/first tenant rather than the permanent home. Surfaced as Extractability NFR in ADR-0038 §5: generic schema field names, configurable paths in scripts, no host-repo-specific assumptions baked into the artifact. Practice question to ask at any cross-cutting design decision: 'would this work as a tenant of itself?' If yes, write it that way from day one — extraction stays cheap. If no, defend why the coupling is permanent. Replaces the implicit 'features live where they're born' default that made the parked Shipyard plan vulnerable to lock-in.
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: implicit 'features live where they're born' default

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Three-layer automation model (Bookkeeping / Pattern-detection / Semantic-content)
userPracticeAdoptions.description: Mental framework for deciding what to automate in any knowledge-management or context-engineering system. Layer 1 (Bookkeeping: dates, fingerprints, scaffolding, file metadata) — automate aggressively; cheap to compute, deterministic, no judgment required. Layer 2 (Pattern detection: recurring recipes, friction signals) — mine-and-propose; machine surfaces candidates, human promotes. Layer 3 (Semantic content: design intent, knownTraps, the "why this is accepted, not a regression" notes) — must stay curated; codebase cannot observe its own intent, closure-capture bugs cannot be derived from line counts. Surfaced from user critique that the new-slice authoring workflow looked like a 7-step manual process. The model is the directional answer: not all of it can or should be automated — but the distinction is now explicit, and every Shipyard tool ships with a Layer-1/2/3 declaration of what it touches. Replaces the implicit 'automate it all' / 'curate it all' false binary.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: This session (commit 759e389 — slice scaffold script auto-fills Layer 1 only; ADR-0038); docs/c-yard/effectiveness-review.md (hypotheses 3 + 4 frozen as testable claims).
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: implicit 'automate it all' / 'curate it all' false binary

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Live-smoke-before-commit verification pattern
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When committing a refactor that crosses a real boundary (external API, third-party service, network protocol), augment hermetic mocked tests with an env-gated live smoke suite that exercises the actual provider. Acceptance is loose — happy-path success OR known acceptable error codes (503/429) both count as green — so the suite stays useful even when quota is exhausted. Pattern proven on ADR-0044 Day 5: live smoke against Gemini caught decommissioned gemini-1.5 fallback models (returned 404 NOT_FOUND) that no hermetic mock would have surfaced, AND let the chain be remediated in the same sprint window before the ADR was promoted to Accepted. Default for any future PR that touches an external integration boundary.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: src/lib/ai/smoke.live.test.ts + scripts/smoke-ai-live.ps1; commit 1472f75; ADR-0044 Acceptance subsection (commit 18c0fbb)
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: hermetic-only test coverage on external-API boundaries

userPracticeAdoptions.name: Hand-author a slice manifest immediately after the feature surface lands
userPracticeAdoptions.description: When a major feature surface ships (an ADR phase completes, a new UI panel goes green), the agent authors the slice manifest in the SAME session while context is at maximum freshness — not later from mined chat exports. Rationale: knownTraps captured in-session carry design intent (the WHY behind a v1 short-circuit, the precedence rule that took 3 turns to converge on) that no analyzer can derive after the fact. Layer-2 mining remains the path for OLD surfaces with no slice; the iron-is-hot pattern is the path for NEWLY-SHIPPED surfaces. Proven this session: docs/c-yard/ai-chat.json (commit 6dc5ef0) authored within minutes of ADR-0046 Phase D.3 landing (commit 22215ce) — captured ~30 hand-authored knownTraps that would have been invisible from transcript mining alone. Default for any future ADR-phase wrap: author the slice (or refresh the existing slice's refreshHistory[]) before writing the handoff.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: docs/c-yard/ai-chat.json refreshHistory[] entry; commits 22215ce (Phase D.3 feature) → 6dc5ef0 (slice manifest); ADR-0046 Acceptance section.

userPracticeAdoptions.name: E→T→R→C ship rhythm (Execute → Test → Review → Commit)
userPracticeAdoptions.description: Behavioral upgrade of the existing E→T→C ship rhythm: a Review step is now inserted between Test and Commit. R = run `npm run review:phase` (column 1 of ADR-0047 three-column review pipeline) and require exit 0 before proceeding to commit. Strict by default; `--accept-net` flag allows per-gate regressions on cleanup PRs if total didn't grow; `vitest.failed > 0` is a hard fail in all modes. R is REQUIRED for phase-end commits, pre-push, ADR-shipping, cross-cutting changes (libs / schemas / types / config). R is OPTIONAL (T still required) for single-file UI tweaks, doc-only commits, scratch experiments. Wall-clock cost ~170s — budgeted as 'slow but cheap insurance against drift.' Locks the regression-detection surface previously hand-rolled on premium agent turns into a deterministic, cacheable, reproducible step.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: user-profile.md memory entry 'E.T.R.C. Workflow Pattern' (this session); ADR-0047 Decision §Workflow integration; commits ef75099 (calibration), 4d5d08d (gate + baseline), 0ed345c (ADR).
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: E→T→C with hand-rolled review on premium agent turns

userPracticeAdoptions.name: ETRC default ship rhythm (E→T→[auto-classify]→R-if-risky→C, always commit-and-queue)
userPracticeAdoptions.description: Behavioural ratchet over the E→T→R→C rhythm adopted yesterday. Previous R = manual full review:phase before commit. New R = mechanical post-commit classifier auto-buckets every commit into trivial/standard/risky; local gemma4:26b runs a design-only check ONLY on risky-tier commits, detached so git commit returns instantly. Every commit auto-logs to docs/review-queue.jsonl (gitignored append-only) for review-day batching. Hard rule: ALWAYS commit-and-queue — no fix-in-loop branch. If R surfaces a design issue, the fix is a separate atomic commit in the next ETC cycle, never an extension of the current commit (preserves bisect/revert/blame cleanliness). Replaces the 'is this commit worth tracking on review day?' in-the-moment decision with mechanical classification at commit-time. Validated against today's session: 9 commits auto-classified live with no perceptual latency.
userPracticeAdoptions.evidenceSource: docs/adr/0049-etrc-rhythm-and-commit-queue.md; docs/workflows/etrc-rhythm.md; commits e739ef8 (feature) + 139d1e5 ({ref} fix) + 6577e09 (Phase 4 wrap); live integration verified — every subsequent commit auto-logged this session.
userPracticeAdoptions.replacedPractice: E→T→R→C with manual review:phase invocation per commit + in-moment 'flag for review?' decisions

infraToolingChanges.name: ADR-0038 Proposed — Slice schema lock + Shipyard Extractability NFR
infraToolingChanges.description: Phase 1 sprint-kickoff ADR. Locks the three open Slice schema decisions from ADR-0037: D1=B (cross-slice relations in docs/c-yard/_index.json adjacency list); D2=B (cross-cutting knowledge stays in user-memory with version-bound vs codebase-bound boundary rule); D3=B (Shipyard repo-only, no scope tiers). Adds D4=B (long-term home is a standalone shipyard/ repo; Resumsify is Phase 1 incubator) and Extractability NFR §5 (no Resumsify-specific names/paths/assumptions in Phase 1 artifacts). G1=A (one slice per UI surface, split at >~15 files). Provisional Phase 1 defaults: fingerprint staleness = warn-and-serve with staleSurfaces[]; evidence schema = { sessions: [{ id, turnExcerpt, toolCallIndex }] }. Phase 1 commit 1 cleared to ship. Same commit also amends ADR-0037 with Decision #7 (long-term home) and Con #6 (extractability tax).

infraToolingChanges.name: Shipyard Phase 1 — Slice unification rollup (5 commits)
infraToolingChanges.description: Phase 1 shipped end-to-end: (1) first slice docs/c-yard/worklog-editor.json + README schema spec [1ff1454]; (2) analyzer --mine-traversals flag for Layer 2 pattern detection [15844f9]; (3) Phase 0 lookup-stack rewrite to consult slice FIRST with mandatory escape-valve audit trail [53204d6]; (4) slice refresh from dry-run evidence — split monolithic knownTrap into 3 sub-bugs, added refreshHistory[] [3362516]; (5) scripts/slice-scaffold.mjs to auto-fill Layer 1 bookkeeping for new slices, cutting cold-start cost from ~45 min to ~3 min curated review [759e389]. Effectiveness hypotheses + review cadence captured at docs/c-yard/effectiveness-review.md.

infraToolingChanges.name: ADR-0044 Proposed — AI provider router (Scope B), 3-layer architecture
infraToolingChanges.description: Week-long sprint kickoff. Scope B locked: consolidate lib/ai.ts + lib/gemini.ts into one façade with task-class routing (5 classes: chat/extract/ground/reason/summarize), add gemini-2.5-pro as premium tier reusing existing GEMINI_API_KEY, stub cost-guard hooks (userId + onUsage emitted but not enforced until multi-tenancy lands). Plug-in provider surface keeps Anthropic/OpenAI/local-models open as future additions. Three-layer architecture committed: L1 Provider Router (this week), L2 Skill Registry (future ADR), L3 MCP Tool Surface (future ADR). Scope C (FirebaseAIProvider/AICoreProvider/BYOK family) documented as Forward Path §1 honoring ADR-0021's Play Store push deferral. No slice manifest written: AI provider is backend infra not UI surface per ADR-0038 §G1; knowledge instead lives in extended AIServicesLayer memory entity. Originally planned as ADR-0022 in conversation; slot taken by worklog Grill Me markdown round-trip; bumped to 0044 to avoid Shipyard's 0039-0043 reservations.
infraToolingChanges.source: docs/adr/0044-ai-provider-router.md; docs/memory/ai-services.json (4 new 2026-06-21 observations on AIServicesLayer)

infraToolingChanges.name: First cross-slice adjacency edge written to docs/c-yard/_index.json
infraToolingChanges.description: docs/c-yard/_index.json gained its first real entry: { 'ai-chat': { 'reads-from': ['worklog-editor/version-history'] } } — because the AI chat code-block 'send to worklog' action shares the WorkLog ContentBlocks write path with the version-history rail. Validates ADR-0038 D1=B (cross-slice relations as a separate adjacency file rather than denormalized inside each slice) by first real use: single-line JSON edit, drift-proof against slug renames (only one place to update), no slice-internal duplication. Mechanism is now load-bearing; future slices append entries the same way. Shipped alongside the ai-chat.json slice in commit 6dc5ef0.

infraToolingChanges.name: npm run review:phase — phase-end OSS regression gate against tracked baseline
infraToolingChanges.description: Self-contained gate script at scripts/review-phase.mjs that re-runs five OSS gates (tsc / eslint / knip / madge / vitest), parses structured counts, and diffs against docs/review-baseline.json. Exits 0 = clean, 1 = regression, 2 = infra/parser failure. Companion npm script `review:baseline` regenerates the baseline. Policy: strict by default; `--accept-net` flag allows per-gate regressions if total across numeric gates didn't grow; `vitest.failed > 0` is a hard fail in ALL modes. Red-team verified: one `any` annotation in an unused src/lib/ file triggers exit 1 with both eslint (+1) and knip (+1) flagging the regression. Initial baseline locks tsc 22 errors / eslint 495 errors + 10591 warnings / knip 0/0/0 / madge 0 circular / vitest 966 passed + 5 skipped + 0 failed (971 total) at commit ef75099. This is Column 1 of the three-column review pipeline (ADR-0047). Workflow recipe at docs/workflows/setup-phase-end-review-gate.md. Backbone for the new E→T→R→C ship rhythm.

infraToolingChanges.name: lefthook pre-push hook — review:phase auto-enforcement (Tier A1)
infraToolingChanges.description: lefthook@2.1.9 installed as devDep; lefthook.yml at repo root configures a pre-push stage that runs `npm run review:phase`. Closes the 'forgot to test before pushing' failure mode — ETC discipline previously depended on user willpower. ~170s gate cost is acceptable because pushes are deliberate events, not per-keystroke. Bypass via `git push --no-verify` documented for emergency. Verified end-to-end on 2026-06-24: `git push --dry-run` fires the hook, gate passes clean, nothing pushed to remote. Single Job, non-parallel, no pre-commit stage (full review:phase is too slow per-commit, perfect per-push).

infraToolingChanges.name: Semgrep Community + 3 seed slice-trap rules (Tier A2)
infraToolingChanges.description: Semgrep installed via `python -m pipx install semgrep` (cross-platform isolated Python env). Wrapper at scripts/review-semgrep.mjs resolves the binary via PATH → ~/.local/bin/semgrep.exe → pipx venv Scripts dir, so it works on any developer machine without PATH config edits. Wired into scripts/review-phase.mjs as hard-fail pre-step (no point grinding tsc/eslint if a slice trap has been re-introduced). Three seed rules under semgrep/rules/: no-window-prompt.yml (WARNING — 56 existing prompt/confirm/alert callsites tracked as Tier B4 debt in /memories/repo/parked-ideas.md); no-radix-onselect.yml (ERROR — zero existing); no-dropdown-trigger-onclick.yml (ERROR — zero existing). Each codified rule converts a Column 2 LLM-caught trap into a Column 1 deterministic gate that fires repo-wide for free. Promotion path: clean up existing callsites then flip `severity: WARNING` → `severity: ERROR` (single-line edit, permanently locks out bug class). First-attempt failures documented in workflow recipe: `tsx` is not a valid Semgrep language (use `typescript`); glob patterns require `**/` prefix for unanchored Semgrepignore-v2; `--severity ERROR --error` is the correct flag combo for ERROR-only gating.

infraToolingChanges.name: Dependabot config — npm + GitHub Actions weekly grouped updates (Tier A3)
infraToolingChanges.description: .github/dependabot.yml shipped: weekly grouped minor+patch npm updates (Mondays 9am ET, max 5 open PRs), majors explicitly ignored to avoid surprise next@17/react@20 mid-sprint, security advisories bypass the schedule and arrive immediately. GitHub Actions ecosystem also enabled for future CI dependency hygiene. Activates only when GitHub sees the config at the repo's remote HEAD — no-push session 2026-06-24 deferred activation to next push. Free, zero-infra, GitHub-native — no contradiction with solo-dev workflow (Dependabot PRs are reviewed + merged in browser, no second-reviewer required).

infraToolingChanges.name: Three-tier review-pipeline strategy ratified (A shipped, B/C/D parked)
infraToolingChanges.description: Strategic synthesis answer to 'how do we build a battle-tested review pipeline as a solo dev.' Honest gap analysis vs industry tools (CodeRabbit/Greptile/Diamond/Codium PR-Agent/Copilot Review/CI/branch protection/SonarQube): all assume multi-contributor PR-based workflow, none fit solo-dev push-to-main. Real leverage gap was enforcement of EXISTING rigor, not new layers. Tier A shipped this session (lefthook pre-push + Semgrep slice-trap rules + Dependabot). Tier B (coverage gate, commit-msg trailer enforcement, weekly review-queue stub, WARNING→ERROR promotions, Semgrep --baseline-commit mode) parked with per-item triggers. Tier C (group-coordination tools) parked with structural rejection — re-evaluate ONLY when second contributor lands. Tier D (DORA-style observability) parked with data-bottleneck triggers. Full roadmap at /memories/repo/parked-ideas.md `Review pipeline — Tiers B/C/D` entry; ADR-0048 ratifies the Tier A architectural commitment.

infraToolingChanges.name: lefthook post-commit hook — non-blocking ETRC advisory layer
infraToolingChanges.description: Added a post-commit stage to lefthook.yml that runs `node scripts/review-log.mjs` on every commit. Non-blocking by hard contract: the script swallows all errors and exits 0 no matter what — a misconfigured hook or crashed classifier never blocks a commit. Hook latency measured at 0.24-0.36s for trivial/standard commits, instant for risky (R-local spawn is detached). Lefthook's `{ref}` template does NOT resolve for post-commit (pre-push/pre-receive only) — my script defaults to HEAD which IS the just-landed commit in post-commit context. First attempt used `{ref}` and emitted a tier:'unknown' queue line; fix shipped as 139d1e5.

infraToolingChanges.name: scripts/review-classify.mjs — mechanical commit classifier (no LLM)
infraToolingChanges.description: Pure Node, no LLM, no network. Given a SHA, examines `git show --shortstat` + changed-file paths to assign tier. Risky triggers: prisma/schema.prisma | migrations | src/app/api/ | src/lib/auth* | src/middleware* | .github/instructions/ | package.json | diff > 300 LOC | src/lib|src/data without test files (TDD-intersect soft signal). Trivial triggers: docs-only | chore(scripts|deps|deps-dev) under LOC | single-file under 30 LOC. Standard otherwise. Hard contract: never throws, exits 0 always, prints tier:'unknown' if it can't determine. Validated against today's 7-commit session: 2/7 (28%) tagged risky = exactly the right ratio (Tier A ship + schema migration). Windows-specific gotcha caught: PowerShell execSync shell=true passes `${sha}^{commit}` through cmd.exe which interprets `^` as escape character; fix is to drop the `^{commit}` suffix entirely (`git rev-parse --verify <sha>` is sufficient for plain SHAs).

infraToolingChanges.name: docs/review-queue.jsonl + reader/escalate scripts — append-only commit-classification queue
infraToolingChanges.description: Append-only JSONL log of every commit's classification + R-local result. Gitignored (per-machine review-day data, not project source). Two line types per SHA: `type:'commit'` with classifier output, `type:'review'` with R-local result. Reader at scripts/review-queue-read.mjs joins entries by full SHA on review-day, tier-filterable (`--tier risky|standard|trivial`, `--since`, `--json`). Manual escalation at scripts/review-escalate.mjs formats commit diff + design-review prompt for paste into a premium subagent (Copilot Opus/Sonnet) when local R said something interesting or nothing useful — pure formatter, no auto-invocation, user decides per-SHA. Three npm scripts: review:classify, review:queue, review:escalate.
infraToolingChanges.source: scripts/review-queue-read.mjs; scripts/review-escalate.mjs; package.json (new scripts); .gitignore (added docs/review-queue.jsonl entry); docs/adr/0049-etrc-rhythm-and-commit-queue.md.

infraToolingChanges.name: scripts/review-r-local.mjs — local gemma4 design-only R for risky-tier commits
infraToolingChanges.description: Fires only for risky-tier commits, detached from the git commit critical path. Calls Ollama gemma4:26b at http://localhost:11434 with a narrow design-only prompt: 'identify ONE structural improvement in <=80 chars (Extract/Move/Reuse/Inline) or reply exactly clean.' Healthcheck-gated against /api/tags (2s timeout); 2-min hard cap on generation. Every failure mode lands a queue entry as `skipped:<reason>` (ollama-unavailable, diff-fetch-failed, ollama-error:<msg>, empty-response, unhandled:<msg>). Joinable to commit entry by full SHA on review-day. v1 prompt observed emitting `skipped:empty-response` on both today's risky commits (small structural diffs with no clear improvement opportunity); v2 prompt tuning parked in ADR-0049 promotion candidates after 5-10 risky commits of data accumulate. Cost: zero $ (local), ~5-120s latency depending on diff size.
infraToolingChanges.source: scripts/review-r-local.mjs; docs/adr/0049-etrc-rhythm-and-commit-queue.md; docs/workflows/etrc-rhythm.md; userMemory:resumsify-lessons.md (Local LLM Workflow Agent gemma4:26b validation 2026-06-14).
